claims.claim: A project scope description can identify deliverables, acceptance criteria, and exclusions, with exclusions helping manage expectations and reduce scope creep.
A deliverable is a unique and verifiable product, result, or capability required to complete a process, phase, or project.
Acceptance criteria are conditions required before deliverables are accepted.
GAO describes scope validation as formalizing acceptance of completed deliverables by comparing actual results with the requirements baseline and documenting validation results.
GAO describes scope control as monitoring project and system scope and managing changes to the requirements baseline, including identifying scope variances and their causes.
An approved or reviewed change should be distinguished from uncontrolled expansion; change itself is not automatically scope creep.
